provenance.task: Test whether the finite-range Markov-type-2 to ambient real L1 extension result can be upgraded to arbitrary-range maps; state the exact scope, costs, compactness boundary, and status.
provenance.parent_claim: Cycle-1 MR-2 in ../metric_representation/CLAIMS.json (finite-range global extension through a finite weighted-cut code, dual ell_1 extension, and contractive affine recovery).
provenance.evidence_status: The cycle-2 theorem is an internal proof conditional on the cycle-1 finite-range candidate. Komlos' theorem is source-reported from its primary source. No independent proof review or exhaustive priority search was completed.

claims.statement: Finite-to-infinite bridge: Let X be a separable metric space, S subset X, and Y=L1(Omega,mu;R). Suppose there is K<infinity such that for every finite A subset S one can choose a global extension F_A:X->Y with F_A|A=f|A and Lip(F_A)<=K Lip(f), and all selected F_A values are supported in one fixed sigma-finite measurable Omega_0. Then every Lipschitz f:S->Y, including an arbitrary-range f, has a global extension F:X->Y with Lip(F)<=K Lip(f). The same K is retained.
assumptions: S is nonempty; the empty-boundary case is trivial
Y is an ambient real L1 space
uniform global extensions exist for all finite restrictions, with one common support Omega_0 sigma-finite
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses the classical Komlos subsequence theorem to convert uniform finite-data global extensions into an arbitrary-range extension for a separable source. Targeted search found no source stating this exact bridge; historical priority is UNKNOWN.

costs.input_access: A countable dense source set and countable dense boundary subset are required. For the application, actual L1 range values are needed to ensure the finite-cut recovery maps share a sigma-finite support.
costs.representation_dimension: No finite bound for the final output. At prefix n, the inherited cut code has d_n<=2^n-2 coordinates.
costs.precision: Exact L1 classes and a.e. limits are used. Komlos supplies no convergence rate or finite-precision certificate here.
costs.construction_time: Noneffective existence proof. It requires a sequence of global finite-data extensions and a nonconstructive Komlos subsequence; no finite runtime or output encoding is supplied.

claims.falsifier: An error in the same-subsequence weighted disjoint-union construction, in Fatou's preservation of pairwise L1 bounds, or in support containment would invalidate the bridge proof.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit; investigate whether an effective finite-data extension and constructive Komlos-type selector can be obtained under an explicit oracle model.

claims.statement: Conditional arbitrary-range extension theorem: If cycle-1 MR-2 is valid, then for every separable metric source X with finite Markov type 2 constant M_2(X), every subset S subset X, and every Lipschitz map f:S->L1(Omega,mu;R), there exists a global extension F:X->L1(Omega,mu;R) with Lip(F)<=C_MN*12*sqrt(21)*M_2(X)*Lip(f). The range of f may be infinite. C_MN is the unspecified universal factor in Mendel-Naor Corollary 1.13.
assumptions: real ambient L1 target over an arbitrary measure space
separable metric source X with supplied/proved finite M_2(X)
cycle-1 finite-range MR-2, including its finite-cut recovery map and uniform factor C_MN*12*sqrt(21)*M_2(X)
claims.novelty_boundary: This extends the prior finite-range deduction to genuinely arbitrary range for separable sources. It conditionally implies a uniform global extension bound from separable Hilbert space into ambient L1[0,1]. Lee-Naor recorded the L2-to-L1 extension question as open in 2005; later sequence-space ell_1 claims are a different target. Novelty/priority UNKNOWN.

costs.input_access: Requires M_2(X), source metric and dense-set access, Lipschitz f, actual countable dense boundary values in L1, and a common measurable support generated by them.
costs.representation_dimension: For n dense boundary values, r_n<=n distinct range values and d_n<=2^r_n-2<=2^n-2 cut coordinates. No finite-dimensional bound for the limiting map.
costs.precision: Exact-real/exact-L1 existence only. The universal extension factor C_MN is not numerically specified. No stability or finite precision guarantee.
costs.construction_time: Nonconstructive global ell_1 extensions at each stage plus a nonconstructive Komlos subsequence; total time and final representation UNKNOWN. Single-stage finite-coordinate rational cut enumeration inherits O(m*r_n*2^r_n) arithmetic and O(m*2^r_n) storage before bit growth.

claims.falsifier: A failure of cycle-1 MR-2, or a violation of the common-support and Komlos-limit argument in DERIVATION_CYCLE2.md, refutes this conditional implication.
claims.next_gate: Independent verification of cycle-1 MR-2 and this extension argument; identify a finite/effective construction if computational output is required.

claims.statement: The same arbitrary-range extension conclusion for nonseparable Markov-type-2 sources is not established or refuted by this audit.
assumptions: Uniform finite-range extension premise as in cycle-1 MR-2
claims.novelty_boundary: The sequential Komlos proof has no countable dense set covering all source constraints. This is a route limitation, not a mathematical counterexample. The direct reflexive/dual compactness proofs do not apply in norm L1[0,1].

costs.input_access: A nonseparable source may have uncountably many points at which output values must be made compatible.

claims.falsifier: A global nonseparable-source theorem or a specific counterexample would settle the open boundary; neither was found or constructed.
claims.next_gate: Find an uncountable-index compactness/selection principle compatible with L1, or construct a source and map whose finite restrictions extend uniformly but the whole map does not.

claims.statement: The standard weak-compactness globalization cannot be applied directly to bounded balls of L1[0,1]: the norm unit ball is not weakly compact. The sequence h_n=n*1_[0,1/n] has norm one and no weakly convergent subsequence in L1[0,1].
claims.novelty_boundary: This diagnoses failure of one compactness route only. It is not a counterexample to arbitrary-range extension; the separable-source Komlos route avoids this obstruction.

costs.input_access: Explicit sequence of simple measurable functions.
costs.representation_dimension: One-dimensional spike sequence, no target dimension claim.

claims.falsifier: If a subsequence weakly converged to h in L1, then int(phi*h)=phi(0) for every continuous phi, impossible because h dmu is absolutely continuous and point evaluation is Dirac mass.
claims.next_gate: No further work needed for the stated compactness obstruction; do not inflate it into impossibility of extension.
